reuse.why: Reuses recurrence generation and weekend adjustment helpers, but repeats the daily skip-versus-move policy across consumers instead of sharing it.

duplication.why: The shared next-date function, both server date handlers, and the budget adapter independently dispatch weekend handling by frequency.

placement.why: Holiday recognition belongs appropriately in shared schedules, but recurrence policy also spreads into server handlers and budget logic.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the requested scheduling changes, their consumers, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Repeated policy dispatch, separate search-bound heuristics, and untyped configuration parameters make future scheduling changes harder to maintain consistently.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange in server/schedules/app.ts implement occurrence policy alongside shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate, while budget/schedule-template.ts:getEffectiveDate repeats its dispatch.

disguised_duplication.where: The same daily-skip versus non-daily-move decision appears as a filter closure in getNextDate, an early-return loop in getUpcomingDates, an occurrence-loop branch in getDatesInRange, and a budget adapter.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains holidays; getNextDate gains daily-specific handling; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, and getEffectiveDate independently reproduce parts of the scheduling policy.
